direction.premise: ШОВ is an interactive physics laboratory for exploring traversable wormhole metrics and understanding how the same observer sees curved space and lensed light.
direction.composition: A large central experiment canvas remains the primary instrument; a compact mode rail spans its top while a separate parameter panel controls the metric and the twin synchronous optics views.
direction.shapeLanguage: Precise orbit arcs and wireframe coordinate lines meet restrained instrument frames, aligned scales and circular photon markers; equations occupy small measurement panels rather than floating decorative tags.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Flat light technical-paper surfaces surround independent Canvas-rendered metric trajectories; the spatial atlas renders wireframe curves while the sky instrument rasterizes calculated optical geodesics.
direction.paletteLogic: A subdued pale background keeps dense numerical controls readable; turquoise highlights selected physics readings, while dark geodesic strokes and bright source markers separate measurement from control.
direction.typography: Compact instrument captions and tabular readouts contrast with one large experiment heading; numerical units such as l/a, H=0 and degrees remain visually adjacent to the controls that generate them.
direction.signature: In the synchronous view, moving the observer relocates the camera marker and simultaneously changes the independently traced gravitationally lensed sky rather than merely rotating a screenshot of 3D.
direction.distinction: Perekos centers live combat aiming in an uninterrupted battlefield, while Rivals Field Notes scrolls through evidence tables; ШОВ keeps the interactive optical measurement and metric model side by side.

architecture.primaryVerb: Change the wormhole metric or observer location, launch photon trajectories and compare a 3D coordinate atlas with the corresponding gravitational lensing view.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Adjusting distance or angle immediately updates displayed numeric readouts and marks the current laboratory state dirty for a new trace; firing the beam adds physically integrated geodesic paths.
architecture.spatialRationale: One large primary experiment stays visible while dense secondary controls occupy a dedicated parameter panel; on narrow phones the two synchronous canvases stack so both instruments retain readable widths.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Rivals Field Notes uses vertically scrolled editorial chapters, filtering and ruled evidence tables; ШОВ uses fixed-height physics canvases and adjacent controls for continuous 3D and optical measurements.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Rivals Field Notes switches hero/season evidence; ШОВ drags a camera, changes real metric parameters and traces new null geodesics in response.

comparisons.spatialDifference: Perekos uses a full-bleed combat stage with perimeter health and movement controls; ШОВ uses a light instrument workbench and two measurable scientific panes beneath a view selector.
comparisons.interactionDifference: Perekos resolves realtime player movement, dodge and spells against an opponent; ШОВ launches photon beams, checks H=0 residuals and records repeatable experiments.

production.renderer: Canvas 2D visualizations calculate and display null geodesics directly, while native HTML controls expose metric parameters without recreating numeric precision in a game texture.
production.focalAsset: The paired 3D geodesic atlas and optically lensed sky are the focal instruments, each regenerated from one shared observer state and explicit metric configuration.

motion.character: Scientific feedback is immediate and anchored to an instrument coordinate system, not springy or character-driven; photons advance along numerical trajectories rather than arbitrary easing curves.
motion.action: A photon-launch button starts a physically integrated bundle whose paths appear on the atlas while the observer window reflects the same starting event.
motion.anticipation: Before a run the selected mode, observer coordinates, beam count and angular spread are already visible next to the action, so the initial conditions can be inspected.
motion.response: The trace count and drawn geodesic paths change when photons are launched; altering the observer changes the location marker and the sampled optical sky.
motion.followThrough: Completed paths and residual checks stay visible until the experiment is cleared; changing view modes preserves the current source settings and recorded experiment conditions.
motion.interruption: Further control changes affect the next generated trace from the current state, while pause and clear commands stop or reset the ongoing experiment without deferred interaction queues.
motion.reducedMotion: Numerical observer coordinates, invariant readings and stopped trajectories remain accessible when animated photon advancement is paused, preserving the scientific conclusions.

evidence.expectedChange: Clicking the launch control adds a photon trajectory from the configured metric and advances the on-screen elapsed time and trajectory count.
